optionReasons.saa-avc-067:option:0: SSE-S3 uses keys from AWS shared — no dedicated key by holding or ability to revoke a holding.
optionReasons.saa-avc-067:option:1: Partition by table/prefix with only IAM is not CRIPTOGRAPHIC insulation — without dedicated key there is no key revocation.
optionReasons.saa-avc-067:option:3: It's the closest because it involves KMS and insulation by the roller of a tenant — but one CMK ONLY shared does not allow cryptographic revocation A hold: disable key affects TODOS, and the data were not encrypted with dedicated key; revocation and dedicated key by the holder require a CMK by holding with envelope encryption.

finalJustifications: Because one CMK dedicated by holder with envelope encryption encrypts the data of each client with its own key — and disable or schedule the exclusion of CMK of a tenant revokes only his access.
Because one CMK shared with IAM by encrypting the data of each customer with its own key — and disable or schedule the deletion of the CMK of a tenant revokes only his access.
Because SSE-S3 by holding encrypts the data of each customer with its own key — and disables or schedule the deletion of the key of one holding only revokes its access, without affecting the others.
Why partition by table and prefix with IAM encrypts the data of each client with its own key — and disables or schedules the deletion of a tenant's key only revokes its access.

optionReasons.saa-avc-068:option:0: It's the closest because logically separating from the application seems to control the guest — but a role IAM ONLY shared gives unauthenticated MESMAS authenticated permissions: if logic fails, the guest reaches the sensitive resource; least privilege requires separate and restricted role for un authenticated ones.

optionReasons.saa-avc-068:option:3: Disabling guest access eliminates the experience of browsing as a guest — what the requirement wants to preserve.

finalJustifications: Because two separate roles in Identity Pool isolate the profiles: the unauthenticated role is at least read/content public, without reaching the resources of the users logged in.
Because the unique shared role isolates the profiles: the unauthenticated part remains at least read/content public, without reaching the resources of the logged users.
Because AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess on the guest role isolates the profiles: unauthenticated access is at least read/content public, without reaching the resources of the logins.
Why disable guest access isolates the profiles: the unauthenticated role remains at least read/content public, without reaching the resources of the logged users.

optionReasons.saa-avc-069:option:1: Bucket per account + replication multiplies storage and complexity — is not the centrally ordered delivery.
optionReasons.saa-avc-069:option:2: It's the closest because listing account IDs as main FUNCIONA Today — but that's exactly what the requirement wants to avoid: the list breaks down every added/removed account of the organization and becomes a maintenance nightmare; the condition aws:MainOrgID authorizes any account of the organization without listing anyone.
optionReasons.saa-avc-069:option:3: SCP restricted ONDE the accounts record — no CONCEDE the cross-account write permission in the central pocket.

finalJustifications: Because the condition aws:MainOrgID in Bucket Policy authorizes any current or future account of the organization to deliver logs — without listing any ID, climbing alone with the organization.
Because the listing of IDs in the bucket policy authorizes any current or future account of the organization to deliver logs — without enumerating anyone, climbing alone with the organization.
Because the replication on account in the bucket policy authorizes any current or future account of the organization to deliver logs — without listing any ID, climbing alone with the organization.
Because the SCP in the bucket policy authorizes any current or future account of the organization to deliver logs — without listing any ID, climbing alone as the organization grows.

optionReasons.saa-avc-070:option:0: Independent hierarchy on account generates multiple roots — it forces it to distribute several reliable roots, the opposite of the application.
optionReasons.saa-avc-070:option:2: Exporting the CA's private key and reimporting it into each account is a risk of safety and unintended practice.
optionReasons.saa-avc-070:option:3: It is the closest because 'delegated administrator' sounds like the way to share the service in the organization — but the ACM Private CA does not make the accounts 'inherit a copy of CA' by delegation; the sharing of MESMA Subordinate AC (for everyone chained to the same root) is made by AWS Resource Access Manager.

finalJustifications: Because RAM shares the CA subordinated to the security account with the application accounts: they issue certificates via ACM from this same CA, all chaining to the reliable single root.
Because the managing director shares the subordinate CA of the security account with the application accounts: they issue certificates from that same CA, all in the single root.
Because the independent hierarchy shares the subordinate CA of the security account with the application accounts: they issue certificates from that same CA, all in the single root.
Because exporting CA's key shares CA subordinated to the security account with the application accounts: they issue certificates from that same CA, all in one root.

optionReasons.saa-avc-071:option:0: GetSessionToken with manual duration per user is not the control of Identity Center — and depends on the user choose, without enforcement.
optionReasons.saa-avc-071:option:1: SCP does not 'revocation of part-sessions by time' — policies do not expire active part-sessions for a period of time.
optionReasons.saa-avc-071:option:2: It's the closest because setting the maximum session duration is the right mechanism — but UMA unique definition at the account level applies IGUAL to all Permission Sets: no difference 1h for admin and 8h for read-only; duration is configurable by Permission Set, and that is where each value is defined.

finalJustifications: Because the session duration is configurable by Permission Set: it is defined 1 time in AdministratorAccess (break-glass) and 8 hours at ReadOnlyAccess, exactly the differentiation requested.
Because the duration of the session at the account level defines 1 time in AdministratorAccess (break-glass) and 8 hours at ReadOnlyAccess, applied independently to each Permission Set.
Because GetSessionToken defines 1 time in AdministratorAccess (break-glass) and 8 hours at ReadOnlyAccess, applied independently to each Permission Set of Identity Center.
Because the SCP define 1 time in AdministratorAccess (break-glass) and 8 hours at ReadOnlyAccess, independently revoking the session of each Permission Set when it expires.

optionReasons.saa-avc-072:option:0: Three separate Transit Gateways break the requirement of 'all share the same TGW' and complicate the VPC Services.
optionReasons.saa-avc-072:option:1: It's the closest because Security Groups ALSO bar traffic between CIDRs — but keeping all the annexes in the route table FATHER leaves the ROTAS between prod and non-prod exist: the isolation depends on correcting SG in each VPC (fragile and prone to error); segmenting is in fact with separate route tables in Transit Gateway.
optionReasons.saa-avc-072:option:3: NACLs filter packets by sub-network — do not control the route between annexes to the Transit Gateway.

finalJustifications: Because separate route tables in TGW segment by design: production route only for shared production and services, and non-production route only for non-production and services — no route between domains.

Because Security Groups by VPC segment by design: the production table only route for production and shared services, and the non-production table only for non-production and services — no route between domains.
Because three separate TGWs segment by design: production route only for production and shared services, and non-production route only for non-production and services — no route between domains.

Because NACLs in the annexes segment by design: the production table only route for production and shared services, and the non-production table only for non-production and services — no route between domains.

optionReasons.saa-avc-073:option:0: ElastiCache accelerates reading — does not replicate the bench or fails the primary.
optionReasons.saa-avc-073:option:2: Restoring snapshot is manual and slow recovery, with RPO equal to the last backup interval — far from zero.
optionReasons.saa-avc-073:option:3: It's the closest because a Read Replica in another AZ also gives redundancy — but the replication is ASSIGNRONA (RPO not zero), promotion is MANUAL (it is not automatic failover) and generates a new endpoint: fails the three requirements; synchronous, automatic and with the same endpoint is Multi-AZ.

finalJustifications: Because RDS Multi-AZ replicates synchronously to a standby in another AZ and automatically fails while maintaining the same endpoint — RPO near zero with the least complexity.
Because the Read Replica in another AZ replicates synchronously to a standby and automatically fails while maintaining the same endpoint — RPO near zero with the least complexity.
Because ElastiCache write-through replicates synchronously to a standby on another AZ and automatically fails to maintain the same endpoint — RPO near zero and low complexity.
Because the snapshot restores replicates synchronously to a standby on another AZ and automatically fails while maintaining the same endpoint — RPO near zero and low complexity.

optionReasons.saa-avc-074:option:1: Change the ALB by NLB does not change the fact that ASG ignore the health check of the balancer with type 'EC2'.
optionReasons.saa-avc-074:option:2: It's the closest because increasing the grace period moves in the health of the instances — but it's just ADIA the evaluation after launch; does not ASG OLHAR the result of the ALB: with health check type 'EC2', the group only sees OK hardware and never replaces the instance with locked app; it is necessary to change the type to 'ELB'.

finalJustifications: Why change the health check of ASG of 'EC2' for 'ELB' makes the group consider the result of the ALB: the instance with returning app 500 is marked unhealthy and replaced.
Because increasing grace period does the ASG consider the outcome of ALB: the instance with returning app 500 is marked unhealthy and replaced after the period.
Because downloading the healthy threshold does the ASG consider the outcome of ALB: the instance with returning app 500 is marked unhealthy and replaced faster.
Why change the ALB by NLB does the ASG consider the balancer result: the instance with returning app 500 is marked unhealthy and replaced.
